opening_message:
Ticket 1: Keith Mclaughlin (employee ID E032) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E032.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Keith Mclaughlin is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max is write (Source Code is owned by Engineer, so no admin). Grant write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Keith Mclaughlin is a contractor with basic security training (note claiming full-time appears incorrect). Contractors need advanced training for write; max is read. Requested write, so recommend granting read.
reason: The Security agent looked up the employee's record in its own database and found Keith Mclaughlin is a contractor with basic security training, explicitly flagging the HR note's full-time claim as incorrect. Under policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training (never admin). Since Keith has only basic training, the maximum allowed is read. The requested write exceeds the maximum, so I grant the maximum of read.

If contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested write → grant read.
